subject: OEM embedding + telemetry / commercial terms (BrightForge)
messages:
From: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop

Hi Karthik —

Quick intro: I’m Arjun (Head of Platform, BrightForge). We’re exploring embedding a hosted or bundled inference capability into BrightForge Designer (desktop + cloud sync). We liked Redwood’s runtime performance and operational controls.

Top-line asks:
- OEM/white-label license (we will ship as "AI powered by BrightForge")
- Metering for usage-based billing to BrightForge customers (can Redwood surface per-customer tokens?)
- Telemetry: we need usage metrics but want to control PII and client identifiers (opt-in).
- Offline/air-gapped support for enterprise customers (how does Private/on-prem differ from Dedicated?)
- Security: SOC2 + audit logging for the inference path

Can you share a short commercial + technical outline? I attached a one-pager asking us to sign an NDA to continue.

Thanks,
Arjun Kapoor
Head of Platform | BrightForge
Arjun@brightforge.ai
Attachment: BrightForge-NDA-request.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop

Arjun —

Thanks for the intro and the NDA. Happy to run through options. Short answers to your bullets first: Hosted/Dedicated/Private map to the choices you described:
- Hosted API: fastest to integrate, Redwood manages runtime, telemetry flows to Redwood (we can surface aggregated metrics to you).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (logical isolation) — we can run a BrightForge-only cluster with SLAs; telemetry is configurable and can be routed to your telemetry store via webhooks.
- Private/on-prem: full control for enterprise customers; supports air-gapped installs with a packaged runtime and a private control plane.

Metering: we support API keys scoped to customer tokens and a usage reporting API — you can pull daily batches or we can push invoices. Telemetry: we support anonymized/hashes of client IDs and an opt-in flag in the SDK for end-customer telemetry.

I attached a short OEM brief that outlines commercial flavors and typical POC success criteria. Would you be available for a 30–45 min call next week so I can bring Vanessa (partnerships) and Neha (security/compliance)? If you can share rough QPS and model sizes (or target model families), that’ll help us recommend Dedicated vs Private.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-oem-brief.pdf

From: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightforge.ai, Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lem@brightforge.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick reply and the brief. Per your ask: approximate estimates below for an initial POC and year 1 forecast (attached).
- POC: 50–200 qps peak, avg 25 qps; model family: open Llama-3 style (7B -> 13B), sequence lengths mostly <1024 tokens.
- Year 1 forecast: 10k unique end-customers, variable usage; monthly aggregate QPS averaging 200–300 with peaks 1k.

Commercial asks:
1) Can Redwood support metering via signed "customer tokens" so BrightForge can mediate billing to its own customers?
2) Telemetry must be opt-in and limited to usage metrics + coarse latency buckets; no raw prompts retained by Redwood for OEM deployments without express consent.
3) BrightForge wants to white-label the UI; Redwood visibility limited to operational dashboards.

We’ve looped procurement on the NDA and attached our usage estimate sheet. Happy to schedule the call — Thurs 21st morning PST works.

—Arjun
Attachment: usage-estimates.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop — summary & ask

Vanessa/Neha —

Looping you both in to kick off commercial and security checks for a potential OEM embedding with BrightForge (see thread below). Quick summary of asks and recommended positions:
- Metering: BrightForge wants to issue per-customer signed tokens. We can support that; recommended: tokens + daily usage push and an integration webhook for reconciliation.
- Telemetry: they require opt-in and no raw prompts retained without consent. Proposed: telemetry opt-in by default off; when on, only store hashed client IDs + latency/size buckets; 90-day retention (open to negotiation).
- Offline: for enterprise customers they want air-gapped support. Recommend Private/on-prem for those customers; Dedicated is good for early POC.
- Legal/commercial: they asked for white-labeling. We should carve out trademark use ("AI powered by BrightForge") and protect model IP.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you prepare a first-pass MPA + MSA redline? Neha — can you confirm SOC2 + audit logging scope and feasibility of 90-day retention? I’ll run the Thurs call with Arjun and Sophie and capture action items.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop — summary & ask

Karthik / Neha / Arjun —

Thanks for including me. From a commercial & partner-ops perspective we can proceed but with the following guardrails I want in the first MPA draft:
- IP/Branding: BrightForge may use co-brand phrase but Redwood retains rights to runtime source and model derivative protections. No re-distribution of runtime as a separate product.
- Telemetry & Data: limit retention to 90 days (we can log events longer for debugging under explicit change control), redact or never store raw prompts for OEM customers unless there is explicit EULA opt-in per end-customer.
- Security: require SOC2 Type II within 90 days of MPA signature (or provide existing attestation and remediation plan).
- POC packaging: recommend Dedicated capacity for 6-month POC with a capped monthly commit; after successful POC transition to either Dedicated reserved or Private deployment for specified enterprise accounts.
- Metering: approve signed customer tokens + daily push; add a reconciliation window of 45 days and capped dispute credits for first year.

I attached our partner onboarding checklist to speed contracting. I’ll draft the MPA redline and share by Fri EOD.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: partner-onboarding-checklist.docx

From: Arjun Kapoor <arjun@brightforge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Interest in embedding Redwood inference in BrightForge desktop — summary & ask

Vanessa / Karthik / Neha —

Appreciate the clarity and the checklist. BrightForge is generally comfortable with the proposed guardrails. A couple of counterpoints from procurement:
- Retention: we can accept 90 days for aggregated telemetry, but for enterprise accounts we request a 180-day option (hosted under BrightForge contract) — is that feasible?
- Pricing cap: for the POC we need a not-to-exceed monthly amount for the Dedicated commit. Please include a POC pricing cap in the MPA redline.

We signed the NDA (attached) — once we have the MPA redline we’ll route to our legal and procurement for a quick turn. Happy to proceed with Thurs call but if you’ve already drafted the MPA, please send that first.

Thanks,
Arjun Kapoor
Attachment: counter-NDA-signed.pdf
